summary.title: Physically Based Rendering: From Theory to Implementation
summary.one_liner: Learn the mathematical theory behind physically based photorealistic rendering and how to implement a full rendering system, using literate programming that combines documentation and source code.
takeaways: Physically based rendering models the physics of light scattering to produce photorealistic images.
The book pairs the mathematical theory of a modern rendering system with its practical implementation.
It uses literate programming, combining human-readable documentation and source code in one reference.
It covers newer material including GPU ray tracing.
The third and fourth editions are freely available online.
summary.summary: This is the website for the textbook Physically Based Rendering by Matt Pharr, Greg Humphreys, and Pat Hanrahan. The page describes the book as a comprehensive guide to the theory and implementation of a modern photorealistic rendering system, presented with literate programming that mixes prose and source code. It notes new coverage of GPU ray tracing and that the book's influence earned the authors a 2014 Academy Award. The page states that the full contents of the third and fourth editions are freely available online. The page text does not list chapters or detailed technical specifics.
